sentences.text: Revenue grew from $4,860.4m in FY2016 [F1] to $14,342.9m in FY2025 [F10], a 12.8% CAGR [F198], but as a spike rather than steady compounding.
FY2021 revenue rose 89.1% to $16,071.7m [D241][F6] on REGEN-COV U.S. sales of $5,828.0m [S48], which the filing ties to a September 2021 U.S. government supply agreement [P39].
FY2022 revenue fell 24.3% to $12,172.9m [D292][F7] as REGEN-COV U.S. sales fell to $0.0m [S49] from $5,828.0m [S48]; the filings cited do not explicitly attribute the decline.
Operating margin peaked at 55.7% in FY2021 [F26] and has fallen four years running to 24.9% [R1][F30].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits, $5,241.6m [S52], was the largest contributor, adding 9.3pp [D592] on 33.6% growth [D591], which the filing ties to higher Dupixent sales [P9].
Net product sales fell 17.3% to $6,309.1m [D506][S16], subtracting 9.3pp from growth [D507].
EYLEA U.S. sales fell 42.4% to $2,747.8m [D577][S43], costing 14.2pp [D578]; the filing cites lower volumes, competition and a lower net selling price [P10].
Operating income fell 10.3% [D441] while revenue grew 1.0% [D440] and operating costs rose 5.4% [D457], a 4.4pp shortfall [D464].
Diluted EPS rose 8.2% [D444] against 2.1% net income growth [D442], helped by a 5.6% lower diluted share count [D459].
Operating margin of 24.9% [F30] is the window low [D749], against a 34.6% median [D751] and 55.7% high [D750].
R&D rose 14.0% to $5,850.2m [D455][X34], reaching 40.8% of revenue [D420] and cutting margin by 4.7pp [D465]; the filings cited do not explain the rise.
Lower SG&A, down 8.6% [D456], added 2.0pp [D466], which the filing attributes to smaller charitable contributions to the Good Days fund [P5].
Pre-tax income of $5,230.7m [X97] equals operating income of $3,577.9m [F20] plus other income of $1,652.8m [X117].
Net margin of 31.4% [F50] sits 6.5pp above operating margin [F30]; the filings cited do not explain the other-income line.
Operating cash flow of $4,978.9m [F80] was 1.11x net income [D428], and free cash flow of $4,080.5m [F100] was 0.91x [D429], near the 0.88x window median [D763].
Free cash flow margin of 28.4% [D425] is above the 26.4% window median [D757] and at the 86th peer percentile [D776].
Capex rose 21.8% to $718.6m in FY2023 [D349][F88], which the filing attributes to Tarrytown and Rensselaer facility expansion [P19].
FY2025 capex of $898.4m [F90] was 1.65x D&A of $543.7m [D430][X67], and stock-based compensation took 20.0% of operating cash flow [D431].
Net cash of $16,879.9m [D434] equals 117.7% of revenue [D435], at the 100th percentile of eight peers [D780] against a -50.7% peer median [D781].
Cash and investments of $18,865.8m [D432] exceed long-term debt of $1,985.9m [F187], and the 4.13x current ratio [F180] is above the 3.97x window median [D766].
Buybacks of $3,438.6m [X137] and dividends of $370.3m [X140], after nil in FY2024 [X139], totalled $3,808.9m [D436], or 93.3% of free cash flow [D437].
Diluted shares fell 5.6% [D459], yet return on average equity of 14.9% [D439] ranks at the 25th percentile of eight peers [D784], against a 38.7% median [D785].
Operating margin has fallen four years running [R1], and the filing ties the FY2025 EYLEA U.S. decline of 42.4% [D577] to competition and lower net pricing [P10].
Receivables still equal 146 days of sales [D438], against 101 days in FY2016 [D19], after a build to $6,036.5m in FY2021 [X193] that the filing ties to REGEN-COV sales [P39].
An operating margin below its 24.9% window low [F30][D749] would extend the decline, while a move toward the 34.6% median [D751] would reverse it; see the FY2026 10-K.
Free cash flow margin falling below the 26.4% window median [D757], from 28.4% [D425], would signal weaker conversion; see the FY2026 10-K.
